messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are whispering, but no one’s ready to shout yet—yet the guards are too relaxed, the money’s slipping out quietly, and the graffiti stays up like a dare. Something’s coming, but not today. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—everyone’s whispering the same things, even when they pretend not to. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 3: "*"The ship’s drifting—even the ones at the wheel don’t seem to know where it’s headed. The streets are talking more than usual, but the money’s drying up, and the usual channels are clogged. Let’s keep our ears open, but stay quiet—this isn’t the time to guess, just to watch."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things are shifting—small signs, but they’re there. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in ways that feel like hesitation, not strength. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our heads down—this could go either way, and we don’t want to be the ones who misread it."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to hide—someone’s checking if the paint will hold, and others are quietly stocking up just in case. The usual noise is still there, but the script’s starting to skip in places. Keep your eyes open, but no need to rush—yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble, just the usual noise. Even the ones who usually know something are shrugging. Might be time to focus on keeping our heads down and our hands steady."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a dam with too much pressure behind it. The cracks aren’t showing yet, but everyone’s bracing for the moment they do. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels tighter than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath but pretending not to. The usual whispers have gone quiet, and the ones who used to push back are suddenly very careful. Not a collapse, but something’s shifting under the surface. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything reckless—yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting louder—people are talking where they used to whisper, and the guards are acting like nothing’s wrong, which is its own kind of answer. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the quiet for safety."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for something to tip the scales. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in the way they move, the way people talk (or don’t), even the way the streets feel. One wrong step—or one lucky break—and things could go either way. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—less like fear, more like something shifting, but no one’s sure if it’s the ground giving way or just the wind changing. The old guard is fraying at the edges, but the military’s still standing tall—so we’ll see which way it leans."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a stack of plates someone’s trying to keep from wobbling. Old connections are stirring, but no one’s sure if it’s because the wind’s changing or just the usual cracks showing. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet—this could tip either way, and we won’t see it coming until it’s already happening."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—like something’s holding, but just barely. The cracks are there, but they’re not breaking yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush. The game’s still in play, but the rules might change fast."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things feel like they’re sitting on a knife’s edge—no one’s backing down, but no one’s moving either. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are showing in weird ways: money’s tight, the streets are quieter in some places, and even the usual loyalists are starting to whisper. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything—this could blow over or blow up, and we won’t know which until it’s too late."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure why. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding slower, and the people who know how to oil them are starting to pack their own tools, just in case. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your hands get too idle."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure which way it’ll go. The old guard’s still holding on, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels still, but not quiet—like the moment before a storm when the birds stop singing. The usual channels are holding, but the cracks are showing in the little things: fewer jokes at the market, more careful glances, and the kind of silence that isn’t peace. Let’s keep our ears open and our circles tight—this calm won’t last forever."*"
Sender 18: "*"The machine is still humming, but the gears are grinding louder than usual—someone’s oiling them, but not everyone’s pulling in the same direction. The streets are quiet, the markets are steady, and the orders keep coming down, but the way they’re delivered feels like a man whistling in the dark. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the noise for movement—yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks yet, but the paint’s fresh in places. The watch groups are talking more than patrolling, and the money’s still flowing, just in different colors. My cousin’s silence worries me, though. Let’s keep our heads down and ears open—this isn’t the time to test the limits."*"
Sender 20: "*"The top is still holding together, but it’s like watching a ship take on water—slow, uneven, and no one’s sure when the pumps will fail. The streets are quiet for now, but the jokes are getting sharper, and the security forces are digging in instead of moving out. If the wind shifts, though, we might all find ourselves in rougher waters than we expected."*"
Sender 21: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure what yet. The usual channels are slower, the elites are hedging their bets, and the streets are too still. Keep your circles tight, but stay ready—this could tip either way, and fast."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking—you can hear it in the whispers, see it in the way they’re scrambling to keep up appearances. But don’t mistake their new ‘legal’ games for weakness; they’re still dangerous, just cornered. Stay sharp, stay quiet, but don’t look away."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels thick—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next gust to decide which way the wind blows. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder, and no one’s sure how long the balance will hold."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like the calm before something, but no one’s sure what. The usual players are moving quietly, the banks are playing it safe, and even the jokes are getting bolder in places they shouldn’t. Not a collapse yet, but the cracks are starting to hum. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could be the lull or the last quiet moment."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the foundation or just the paint. Old friends are whispering again—some out of hope, some out of fear—but the regime’s own people seem to be holding their breath too. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
